question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

It is 2036. Looking back, 5 landmark papers each settled this question in a way that surprised the field, because of how they approached it. For each paper, describe what it measured, analyzed, or did, as a concrete idea a research lab could pursue today. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Persistence of enhancer occupancy after stimulus washout
ideas.description: Knock in endogenous HaloTag or degron-tagged FOS and JUN, then track single-cell AP-1 occupancy and enhancer accessibility by live imaging and CUT&Tag for days after a transient stimulus is removed. Memory requires that occupancy or chromatin state outlast both the signal and the transcriptional output, so a decoupling of these timescales would be the key result.

ideas.title: Acute depletion after an optogenetic AP-1 pulse
ideas.description: Drive FOS:JUN activity with a light-inducible dimerization system for a short pulse, then acutely degrade AP-1 with an auxin-inducible degron at a later time point. If the downstream gene program and enhancer state are maintained without AP-1 present, the response is self-sustaining, which is the core of a memory mechanism.

ideas.title: Mitotic inheritance of AP-1-induced states via lineage barcoding
ideas.description: Barcode cells with lentiviral lineage tags, apply a single AP-1 pulse, and use paired single-cell ATAC and RNA profiling to follow the response through multiple divisions. Quantifying how many generations the enhancer state and transcriptional response persist, with and without Polycomb or H3K27ac perturbation, tests whether memory is transmitted through cell division.

ideas.title: Mitotic bookmarking and faster re-activation
ideas.description: Use live imaging of tagged FOS and JUN through mitosis to measure whether AP-1 stays bound to chromosomes, then compare how quickly target enhancers reopen in daughter cells with and without retained bookmarks. Depleting candidate bookmarking factors would show whether retention is required for the faster reactivation.

ideas.title: Savings test in tissue with sequential stimulation
ideas.description: In mice, deliver a first AP-1-driving stimulus, wait weeks to months, then deliver an identical second stimulus and measure re-induction speed and magnitude of target genes and chromatin opening using a time-stamped reporter. A faster or stronger second response, independent of the first stimulus's direct effects, is the in vivo signature of memory that the field would need to accept.
